deeper.title: What the price assumes
deeper.text: The price assumes about 28% a year growth in free cash flow for 10 years, then 3% (discount rate 9.9% = 10-year Treasury 4.9% + 5%; base: sales × its 3-year median free-cash margin (5%), because current free cash flow is negative). For comparison, sales grew 22% last year; 12%/yr over 3 years — the market expects faster growth than the company has recently delivered.

deeper.title: Return on capital
deeper.text: 49% — each $100 invested in the business (debt + equity, net of cash) earns about $49 a year after tax; return on shareholders' equity 28% (3 years ago 396%). (Tax rate estimated at 21%: effective rate not reported.)

deeper.title: Signed future revenue
deeper.text: Signed but not yet delivered (remaining performance obligations): $664.0B, up 46% from a year ago — about 9.3× the last 12 months of sales; customer prepayments not yet earned (deferred revenue): $30.8B, up 130% from a year ago.

deeper.title: Multi-year view
deeper.text: Sales grew 12%/yr over 3 years and 0%/yr over 5 years; operating margin today 32% vs a 5-year range of 14–32% (median 29%): near the top of its range (cycle peak risk: margins this high often fall back).

tiles.title: Profit margins
tiles.read: Each $100 of sales leaves $32 of operating profit, about the same as a year ago.
tiles.explain: Operating margin = operating profit ÷ sales. Gross margin = what's left after the direct cost of the product.

tiles.title: Free cash flow
tiles.read: Free cash flow is negative: it's spending more (often on new capacity) than the business brings in.

tiles.explain: P/E = share price ÷ earnings per share. Forward P/E uses next year's forecast earnings.
